questions.q: Describe the useful and harmful roles of microorganisms.
answer: Microorganisms are tiny living things, seen only under a microscope, and they affect us in both helpful and harmful ways.

answer.text: Lactobacillus turns milk into curd and yeast is used to make bread and alcohol. Rhizobium and blue-green algae fix nitrogen and enrich the soil. Antibiotics such as penicillin, and vaccines, help fight disease, and decomposers recycle nutrients by breaking down dead matter.

Some microbes, called pathogens, cause diseases — bacteria cause tuberculosis and cholera, viruses cause colds and polio, the protozoan Plasmodium causes malaria spread by the female Anopheles mosquito, and fungi cause skin infections. Others spoil food or cause food poisoning.

answer: Good hygiene, clean water, vaccination and food preservation help control the harmful ones.

questions.q: How are microorganisms classified, and where are they found?

answer.text: are living things too small to be seen without a microscope, and they are grouped into main types.

list: Bacteria — single-celled organisms found almost everywhere
Fungi — such as moulds and yeasts
Protozoa — such as amoeba and the malarial parasite
Algae — simple plant-like organisms; and viruses, which act as living only inside a host

answer.text: Microbes are found in air, water, soil, inside and on the bodies of plants and animals, and even in extreme places like hot springs and icy regions.

list: This wide presence is why they play such large roles, both helpful and harmful

questions.q: How do microorganisms help in making food and medicines?

answer.text: in food and medicine, turning them into valuable helpers.

list: Yeast is used in baking bread and in brewing, where it ferments sugar and releases carbon dioxide that makes dough rise
Microbes are used to make cheese, pickles and other fermented foods
Antibiotics such as penicillin are made from fungi and bacteria and kill disease-causing microbes
Weakened microbes are used to make vaccines that build immunity against diseases
